question.text: A rat is running on ice with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Suddenly he decides to turn by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and want to keep running with the same speed throughout. What is the least amount of time (in seconds) he needs for such a turn? Suppose that rat’s feet can move independently. Coefficient of friction between rat’s feet and ice is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>125</mn></math>. (Given: <math><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></semantics></math> )
